chunks: And from him, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said:

I asked him about a man who said, 'The first slave I acquire is free.' He did not long before he acquired six [slaves]. Which of them should he free? He said, 'He draws lots among them, then frees one.'

And I asked him about a man who marries his female slave to a man and says, 'The first child she bears to him is free.' The man died, and another man married her, and she bore him children. He said, 'As for [the children] of the first [husband], they are free. And as for [the children] of the second, if he wishes, he may enslave them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing one slave when a man has multiple slaves, and the status of children from a freed female slave's second marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanics of *itq* (emancipation) by establishing that if a master frees a specific slave but acquires more, he must use lots (*kura*) to select the freed one, ensuring fairness. In the second scenario, it distinguishes between the offspring of the designated wife (who is free) and those from a subsequent marriage (who remain enslaved), highlighting the legal principle that the master's right to retain or free depends on the specific contractual conditions set at the time of the wife's marriage. These rulings reflect the Shia juristic emphasis on precise intent (*niyyah*) and the distinct legal status of *ummahat al-awlad* (mothers of children) in determining generational freedom.
